recommendation: Keep the empty audit commit as-is. No FHIR-core edit is needed for FHIR-17630 unless the work group later reopens the broader timezone policy; FHIR-16550 should remain background for this seed rather than a separate opportunistic decision.
issue_request: FHIR-17630 was Published/Persuasive for R5 as a follow-up to FHIR-16550. It requested a link to draft-sharhalakis-httptz-05, SHOULD-level client population and server use of the client-timezone header, and client timezone population when communicating dates so server-local defaults do not surprise users.
initial_application: FHIR-16550 added the date-search cautionary note in source/search.html through commit 7310bd4a428c. FHIR-17630 was explicitly applied by commit 77f262f2638f99b947ab5ba72761d95b065b339d, which added the Client Timezone section to source/http.html; later editorial commits adjusted wording and conformance wrappers without removing the approved substance.
additional_context: FHIR-I minutes from 2019-04-15 confirm the 11-0-0 decision to point to the rejected IETF client timezone draft rather than invent a FHIR-specific header. The linked #implementers Zulip thread shows the policy was intentionally cautious because offsets, timezones, server locality, and clinical-event locality can differ.
reconciliation: No source change was made. source/http.html already links to the draft RFC, notes it was not adopted, and says clients SHOULD always populate the header while servers SHOULD use it; source/search.html already says clients SHOULD provide a timezone when the time part is present and retains the timezone correction caveats.
